observations: The runtime gave me no subagent or task ID, so reviewer.task is null. Files I read: AGENTS.md (via CLAUDE.md), docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md, docs/PROMPTS.md, this request (script for page 01, boundary page 02 and the embedded first reading), source/original.txt and source/REVISION-2026-11-11.md. Images I opened with Read and looked at myself: workflow/review/page-01.png, page-02.png (outgoing boundary) and assets/panels/02-4.png. Every file opened without error.

Wording matches the source and script exactly. 01-1 caption: 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' 01-2 Meera: 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...' and 'I wish everything were easier to manage!' The source's single line is split into two balloons with no words changed. 01-3 Ananya: 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.'

01-1: the caption box sits at the top left over sky, leaves and the left end of the awning. Ananya's face (about y 170-230) is below it, and her open left-hand gesture, the elderly patient and the seated patients are all clear. The panel has no balloons.

01-2: balloon 1 is at the top left. Its tail runs over plain wall to the top of Meera's hair. Balloon 2 is lower and to the right, and its short tail ends above her head, beside the drawn strain marks without covering them. Her face, the receiver, the pen hand, the bangle, the open register and the stacked registers are all clear of lettering. Higher-left before lower-right gives the list first and the wish second.

01-3: the single balloon sits on plain wall at the top. Its tail ends at Ananya's hair above her face, and her chin hand, stethoscope and coat hand are clear. Meera, small in the background, has no lettering on her, so the speaker is unambiguous.
All text is set in a clear, even font in uncrowded balloons. Nothing is too small at page size.

Scanning without guides, I read the top-tier caption, then the lower-left panel's top-left balloon, then its lower-right balloon, then the lower-right panel's balloon. The two 01-2 balloons are stepped (the second starts about 95 px lower), so the eye does not jump to 01-3's balloon at the same height before reading Meera's second line. The gutter and the separate panel frame keep 01-3's balloon apart.
No balloons from different speakers sit close enough to be confused. Meera's two balloons are one speaker's continuous thought, so reading them as a pair loses nothing.

transitions.observation: Outside to inside the same clinic. 01-1 shows the reception desk with the phone and registers through the glass door, and 01-2 cuts to that desk with Meera on the phone. The queue of patients' backs carries the 'busy day'.
01-3 shows the same desk in the background with Meera still on the phone writing, while Ananya watches with her hand at her chin. Her line follows straight from Meera's wish.

From the morning reception to the evening office. Ananya's 'Let's make the rest simpler' sets up the onboarding as her response. On page 02 the sunset window (02-1, 02-2) and the caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' mark the new step, and the 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic' label names the product. The source fixes this caption wording, and no time word is needed for the step to be understood.

readingReview.comparison: The first reader's order (caption, list, wish, Ananya's resolution) matches the script order exactly, and their tail and coverage findings agree with mine. Their ambiguities: (1) Meera voicing the complaint with the receiver at her ear reads as an exasperated aside during a hectic call. The source places the line in exactly this moment ('a ringing phone, and Meera managing a queue'), and the tails leave no doubt about the speaker, so this is acceptable. (2) Ananya speaking with nobody visibly listening: the source specifies that she 'looks thoughtfully at the reception desk'. 'Let's' makes it a resolution for the clinic, not a reply to Meera, and page 02 shows it carried out. This is acceptable as intended. (3) Identification through the caption plus the white coat is enough, as the reader said. The hair difference they noted in panel 1 is an artwork matter, not lettering. In 01-1 her hair is pinned up with loose strands, consistent with the low bun plus strands in the cast description. Nothing is skipped or unresolved.
